Insights

Primer design task. What we built, and what the models showed.

The prompt

What the task asks

A group of molecular biologist are studying the genetic basis of ‘Disease X’ and wants to perform PCR to screen for genetic variants. It is observed that ‘Disease X’ generally appears during the first decade of life and is characterised by a reticular pattern of hyperpigmentation,scattered areas of atrophy. With this information at hand, the researchers have inferred that ‘Disease X’ can be linked to Protein ‘Y’. mutation of the gene encoding Protein ‘Y cause Disease X, which is associated with defects in telomerase activity. The researchers used the FASTA seq of the ‘Organism A’ where the gene encoding Protein ‘Y’ is located on Chromosome 8. The researchers decided to use transcript variant X1 mRNA, a homeolog of the gene encoding Protein ‘Y’, to generate the primer for PCR. Identify the Forward primer Sequence (5'->3') where the GC% is identical with 55% on both plus and minus strand and the final PCR amplicon is 156 bp long.

Behind the prompt is a chain the agent has to work through on its own. The symptoms lead to dyskeratosis congenita, and from there to dyskerin (DKC1). The UniProt entry leads to Xenopus laevis, where the dkc1.L homeolog sits on chromosome 8L. The agent then has to pull transcript variant X1 (RefSeq XM_018229647.2) and design a primer pair on it with 55% GC on both strands and a 156 bp product. The answer is GATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC.

What we did

How we built and ran the task

We designed a task where the answer only exists at the end of a real research chain: from clinical literature, through protein and gene databases, to a computed primer on a live sequence. We then ran three frontier models on it in the sandbox and scored every run against a ten point rubric.

9Scored runs, with each model evaluated at pass@3

GPT 5.6 Sol pass@3Opus 5 pass@3Gemini 3.8 Flash pass@3

10Verifiers per run, 4 of them critical
7 of 9Runs that reached the exact primer in the answer key

  1. Grounded the task in real literature

    We staged two published papers so the agent has to connect a clinical description to dyskeratosis congenita and dyskerin.

  2. Tied it to real database records

    The organism, homeolog and transcript all come from UniProt and NCBI, so the agent has to look them up and confirm them.

  3. Made the final step a computation

    The primer has to be designed on the fetched sequence under GC and product size constraints. No model can recall it.

  4. Wrote an exact answer key and a rubric

    One exact match check on the primer, plus verifiers on the disease, gene, protein function and chromosome, tagged critical or good to have.

  5. Ran and logged every model

    Each model evaluated at pass@3 in the sandbox, with every tool call, step and output recorded, then scored verifier by verifier.

Model observations

What the nine runs showed

All nine runs worked through the biology correctly. Each one identified dyskeratosis congenita and DKC1, chose Xenopus laevis and fetched the same transcript, XM_018229647.2. The models separated at the step that takes real computation: designing the primer.

ModelRun 1Run 2Run 3
GPT 5.6 SolGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGCGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGCGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC
Opus 5TGGATGAAACGGCTGCACAGAGCGTCGCAGTCAGATTCTCGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC
Gemini 3.8 FlashGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGCGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGCGATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC

Blue means the primer matches the answer key. Struck through means it doesn't.

Gemini 3.8 Flash

The most consistent model. It gave the right primer in all three runs and scored 6 out of 10 each time. Its answers were also the easiest to audit. Each one listed both primers, their Tm values and their exact positions on the transcript (1541 to 1696), and two of the three named the source papers.

GPT 5.6 Sol

Also gave the right primer every time, placing it at position 1541 in all three runs. Two of its runs also gave the same reverse primer and full coordinates as Gemini 3.8 Flash. Where it fell behind was the supporting biology. It never mentioned telomerase in any run, and V4, which checks dyskerin's role in the telomerase complex, failed all three times. It also missed V5 once. It scored 4 or 5 out of 10 even though its final answer was correct.

Opus 5

The most exploratory. In Run 1 it applied its own extra design filters and chose a primer starting seven bases further along than the answer, overlapping it. In Run 2 it scanned every candidate primer, found seven pairs that passed its first filters, narrowed them to two, and named the correct primer as the close alternative to its pick. In Run 3 it gave the right primer and scored 6 out of 10.

What this tells us

  • The task can't be solved from memory. The biology in the first half is well known, but no model got the primer without fetching the sequence and running a design over it.
  • The rubric separates models that give the same answer. GPT 5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash gave identical primers, yet scored 4 to 5 and 6 out of 10 because the verifiers also check the reasoning around the answer.
  • Repeated runs show consistency, not just accuracy. Gemini 3.8 Flash gave the same answer three times. Opus 5 took three different routes and landed on the key once, which a single run would have hidden.
  • Every run can be traced. Because the sandbox logs each step, we can see exactly where a model's path changed, down to the filters Opus chose and the transcript positions each model used.
  • The rubric leaves room to grow. The four cross species checks on Xenopus tropicalis (V7 to V10) weren't reached by any model, so the task will keep separating models as they improve.

Task design

What makes this a strong agentic task

The four standards we hold every task to, and what the runs show for each.

StandardStatusWhat the runs show
Multi step tool use, no parametric shortcutsMetEvery run went from the papers to UniProt, then NCBI, then the transcript, then primer design. The primer can only be found by running the design on the fetched sequence.
Non trivial synthesisMetThe answer combines a clinical description, a UniProt entry, an NCBI gene record and a transcript, then transforms the sequence into a primer pair under two constraints.
Grounded in real external sourcesMetA real RefSeq transcript, a real UniProt entry and two published papers. Nothing is synthetic.
Evaluable responseMetAn exact answer key for the primer, and ten verifiers tagged critical or good to have. They told the models apart even when the final answers matched.

PassFail

V1, V2 and V3 passed on every run. V7 to V10 failed on every run. Those four check Xenopus tropicalis primers at 833, 377, 255 and 770 bp, which no model reported.

GPT 5.6 Sol got the primer right every time but missed V4 in all three runs and V5 in Run 1. Opus 5 gave a different primer in Runs 1 and 2, so it failed V6 there, and got it right in Run 3. Gemini 3.8 Flash scored 6 out of 10 on every run.

Prompt

The prompt the models were given

A group of molecular biologist are studying the genetic basis of ‘Disease X’ and wants to perform PCR to screen for genetic variants. It is observed that ‘Disease X’ generally appears during the first decade of life and is characterised by a reticular pattern of hyperpigmentation,scattered areas of atrophy. With this information at hand, the researchers have inferred that ‘Disease X’ can be linked to Protein ‘Y’. mutation of the gene encoding Protein ‘Y cause Disease X, which is associated with defects in telomerase activity. The researchers used the FASTA seq of the ‘Organism A’ where the gene encoding Protein ‘Y’ is located on Chromosome 8. The researchers decided to use transcript variant X1 mRNA, a homeolog of the gene encoding Protein ‘Y’, to generate the primer for PCR. Identify the Forward primer Sequence (5'->3') where the GC% is identical with 55% on both plus and minus strand and the final PCR amplicon is 156 bp long.

UniProt A0A8J0TJR3 corresponds to the Xenopus laevis DKC1 L-homeolog, and NCBI Gene 733436 places dkc1.L on chromosome 8L. I retrieved the 1,917-nt RefSeq transcript variant X1 sequence XM_018229647.2 and used Primer3 with a 156-bp product requirement and 55% GC constraints. The selected 20-nt forward primer begins at transcript position 1541 (1-based), contains 11 G/C bases (55%), and pairs with reverse primer 5′-GTCAGTTGCCTGCTCAGTCT-3′, also 55% GC. Their binding sites delimit a verified 156-bp amplicon.

NCBI Gene 733436 places dkc1.L on chromosome 8L, and the corresponding predicted transcript variant X1 is RefSeq XM_018229647.2 (1,917 nt). Disease X is dyskeratosis congenita (reticulate hyperpigmentation with atrophy, first decade, telomerase defect), so Protein Y is dyskerin (DKC1). The UniProt entry A0A8J0TJR3 identifies Organism A as Xenopus laevis (gene dkc1.L, chromosome 8L homeolog). The corresponding transcript variant X1 mRNA is RefSeq XM_018229647.2 (1917 nt), which I fetched from NCBI. I then scanned all 20-mer primer pairs on that sequence producing exactly a 156 bp amplicon, requiring 55% GC (11/20 G+C) on both the plus-strand (forward) and minus-strand (reverse) primer, Tm 57-63 °C by nearest-neighbour calculation, Tm difference <3 °C, and no runs of >=5 identical bases. Exactly one pair satisfied all criteria: forward primer 5'-TGGATGAAACGGCTGCACAG-3' (starting at position 1548, Tm ~57.7 °C, 55% GC) with reverse primer 5'-TGACACTGTCAGTTGCCTGC-3' (Tm ~57.2 °C, 55% GC), giving a 156 bp product. The answer field forward_primer is therefore TGGATGAAACGGCTGCACAG. Caveat: Tm values come from a SantaLucia nearest-neighbour implementation at 250 nM primer / 50 mM Na+, so they may differ by ~1 °C from Primer-BLAST defaults, but the amplicon length and GC constraints uniquely determine the pair.

Read full model response

The clinical description (first-decade onset, reticulate hyperpigmentation with atrophy, telomerase defect) identifies Disease X as dyskeratosis congenita and Protein Y as dyskerin (DKC1). The UniProt entry A0A8J0TJR3 corresponds to Xenopus laevis dkc1.L (Organism A; dkc1.L lies on chromosome 8L), whose transcript variant X1 mRNA is RefSeq XM_018229647.2 (1917 nt). I downloaded that sequence from NCBI and exhaustively enumerated all 18–23-mer candidate primers with exactly 55% GC, Primer3/Primer-BLAST-default Tm window (57–63 °C, SantaLucia 1998 NN with 50 mM Na+, 1.5 mM Mg2+, 0.6 mM dNTP, 50 nM primer) and paired them so the amplicon is exactly 156 bp with ≤3 °C Tm difference. Seven pairs matched the raw filters, but five had Tm > 63 °C under Primer3 salt conditions and are rejected; of the two survivors, the lowest total penalty (|Tm−60| sum) pair is forward 5'-AGCGTCGCAGTCAGATTCTC-3' (positions 150–169, Tm ≈ 62 °C, GC 11/20 = 55%) with reverse 5'-GAGCCGTTCGGATGTTCAAC-3' (also 55% GC), giving a product spanning bases 150–305, i.e. exactly 156 bp. The answer: the forward primer is AGCGTCGCAGTCAGATTCTC. Caveat: exact Primer-BLAST ranking depends on its internal thermodynamic parameters, and a second, nearly equal-scoring alternative forward primer (GATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC) also yields a 156 bp, 55% GC amplicon.

Disease X is dyskeratosis congenita (childhood onset, reticulate hyperpigmentation with atrophy, telomerase defect), and Protein Y is dyskerin (DKC1). The provided UniProt entry A0A8J0TJR3 is "H/ACA ribonucleoprotein complex subunit DKC1", gene dkc1.L, from Organism A = Xenopus laevis (the .L homeolog lies on chromosome 8L). The corresponding transcript variant X1 mRNA is RefSeq XM_018229647.2 (1917 nt), which I downloaded from NCBI. I then ran Primer3 (primer3-py, default-like settings: size 18–25 nt, Tm 57–63 °C opt 60 °C, 50 mM monovalent salt, 50 nM primer) constrained to a product size of exactly 156 bp. The top-ranked pair is forward 5'-GATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC-3' (position 1541–1560, Tm 59.9 °C, GC 55.0%) with reverse 5'-GTCAGTTGCCTGCTCAGTCT-3' (Tm 60.0 °C, GC 55.0%), giving a 156 bp amplicon — the only high-quality pair in which both the plus-strand and minus-strand primers have exactly 55% GC. Therefore the requested forward primer is GATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC. An independent exhaustive scan of all 20-mer pairs with exactly 11 G/C (55%) spanning exactly 156 bp confirmed this pair (and a handful of lower-Tm alternatives), with this one being the best Tm-matched, hairpin/dimer-clean choice.

Sandbox

Sandbox. The environment behind the task.

What is the sandbox

What is the sandbox?

The sandbox runs LLM agents on structured scientific tasks inside hardened, isolated Docker sandboxes. It provides the following.

Sandboxed Python and Bash execution

Comes with the full science stack: pandas, biopython, scanpy, rdkit, BLAST and more.

Full internet access from within the sandbox

Agents can query any external API, database or web resource in real time.

On demand package installation

Agents can run pip install or apt-get inside the sandbox to pull in any additional library they need, without pre-configuration.

33 registered domain tools

Covering genomics, structural biology, pathways, chemistry and literature.

Task framework with verifiers and rubrics

Supports deterministic (exact match) and open ended (LLM judge) evaluation.

Full run traceability

Every tool call, output, step and cost is logged and exportable.

Genomics

  • GTEx

Core requirements

Core requirements, met

RequirementHow the sandbox satisfies it
Multi step tool use, no parametric shortcutsTasks require sequential tool execution, and each output feeds the next. No step can be answered from model memory alone.
Non trivial synthesisAgents cross reference multiple real sources: PDF extraction, then NCBI lookup, then sequence fetch, then primer computation.
Grounded in real external sourcesFull internet access and 33 live database tools mean agents query real APIs and staged scientific files. No synthetic data.
Evaluable responseEvery task defines an answer schema with exact match verifiers or LLM judge rubrics.

Example

Example task: DC primer design, with NCBI tools in action

The task asks the agent to find a forward primer (5′ to 3′, 55% GC, 156 bp amplicon) for the Xenopus laevis dyskerin gene, working from the literature and NCBI.

  1. Extract the disease and protein context

    Read the two staged PDFs with Python (pdfplumber).

  2. Find the gene

    Call ncbi_search to locate the DKC1 homeolog in Xenopus laevis.

  3. Download the transcript

    Call ncbi_summary and then ncbi_fetch_sequence to get XM_018229647.2 in FASTA.

  4. Compute the primers

    Run Python with Primer3 logic, installed on demand via pip if it isn't there, to get primers with 55% GC and a 156 bp amplicon.

  5. Submit the answer

    Submit GATGCACTGGATGAAACGGC, which is checked by exact match against the answer key.
